citation: Dubey V, Darlow C, Gerada A, Unsworth J, Sheth E, Reza N, Farrington N, Haldenby S, Warren D, Liu X, Howard A, Hope W, et al. Molecular pharmacodynamics of amoxicillin-clavulanic acid for urinary tract infections caused by Escherichia coli. Nature Communications 2026;17(1).
file: 41467_2026_74323_MOESM4_ESM.xlsx, the article Source Data file, stored here as source_data.xlsx
why_this_deposit: The only deposit found in an overnight search of five repositories, the TB consortia, the persistence literature, food microbiology and the hollow-fibre field that carries all three fields the boundary framework needs: a plated volume from which the floor is DERIVED, measured per-culture starting densities rather than a nominal inoculum, and raw counts with below-limit readings retained as a placeholder rather than deleted.
floor: L = 10 CFU/mL, from 100 uL plated with counts reported per mL. Corroborated inside the file: all 229 genuine counts are exact multiples of 10 and the smallest is exactly 10.
known_quirks: Entries of exactly 1 in the drug-treated columns are the below-limit placeholder, not counts; a 100 uL plate cannot return 1 per mL.
Column headers say 'log10 CFU/mL' but the columns hold linear CFU/mL.
The Methods give a nominal inoculum of 1e5 CFU/mL; the measured t=0 counts are 7e5 to 2.8e6, so using the nominal figure would put a full order of magnitude into every boundary.
The drug-treated arm reads at or below the limit already at t=0 while its paired control reads about 1e6, so that sample was taken after exposure rather than before.
